Subject: Order form invoicing entity and withholding question

Marcus —

Thanks for the call earlier. A couple of follow-ups from our side so procurement can issue the PO:

- We need invoices to be issued to our EU entity: "StellarNet Europe B.V." (NL VAT ID: NL123456789B01). Please confirm Redwood can issue invoices to an EU entity.
- Our finance team will need an official tax residency / withholding certificate from Redwood if we are required to withhold local taxes. In the Netherlands, withholding rates for software services vary; our team is planning to withhold 3% pending evidence.
- Net terms: our standard is Net60, but we can accelerate to Net45 for approved vendors. Can Redwood confirm Net45 is acceptable for this deal?

If you can send a redlined order form that includes an invoicing entity field and a tax clause, we will review and return with a PO.

Thanks — attaching our standard AP contact for record.

Best,
Elena

Subject: Re: Order form invoicing entity and withholding question

Elena —

Thanks for the clear notes. Appreciate the heads up on the EU entity. Short answers up-front:

- We can issue invoices to StellarNet Europe B.V.; we do that for a number of EU customers. We will need the invoice-to legal name + VAT ID on the PO.
- Redwood’s standard position is that the customer is responsible for any withholding tax; we can provide a tax residency / certificate document on request so you can apply the correct domestic relief. We do not gross-up for withholding as a standard practice, but we can escalate if this is a blocker.
- Net45 is within our usual accepted terms for order forms. I’ve flagged Finance for the Net60 conversation but expect Net45 should be fine for this deal size.

I’m looping in Kimberly (Finance lead) and Ben (Sales Ops) to propose an order form redline that adds: (1) invoice entity selection, (2) clear tax withholding language, and (3) a payment-tranching waterfall so that invoicing lines and activation fees are unambiguous.

Attaching a working draft (order_form_v3_redline.pdf) — it has placeholders we can fill after you confirm invoice-to details.

Next steps I propose:
1) StellarNet confirms invoice-to legal name, VAT ID and whether you will issue a PO.
2) Redwood returns final redline and a DocuSign-ready order form.
3) You send PO + tax certificate; first invoice triggered on signature / activation per redline waterfall.

If you prefer a quick call tomorrow to close entity details, I can schedule 15–20 minutes.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Order form invoicing entity and withholding question — proposed redlines

Hi Elena —

Thanks for the details. I took a pass at legal redlines and added a short carveout for invoicing / withholding that should align with your procurement needs while preserving Redwood’s standard commercial protections. High-level items included: 

- Invoice entity clause: an explicit "Invoice-To" field in the order form. Customer can elect an alternate invoice entity; Redwood will supply the corresponding tax documentation if requested.
- Withholding / Gross-up: Customer is responsible for any withholding taxes under local law. If withholding reduces the net payment below the agreed amount, the parties will follow the order form process to either (a) apply gross-up (by written agreement) or (b) accept a net payment and adjust future invoices. We included a mechanism to request a gross-up exception in writing.
- Tax certificates: Redwood will provide a tax residency certificate (or equivalent) within 5 business days of a written request from the customer.
- Payment waterfall: first invoice due on signature (activation fee), recurring invoices monthly in arrears; we added language to support splitting invoices across entities where needed (e.g., EU entity for tax authorities).

I attached the redlined PDF and a clean copy with tracked "Invoice-To" placeholders. If the StellarNet AP team can confirm the exact legal name and VAT ID, we will populate and prepare a DocuSign envelope.

DocuSign draft: https://www.docusign.com/link/to/redlined-orderform
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/43521/rdw-2027-str-0421

If any of the proposed text is problematic from your side (e.g., you require automatic gross-up), we can escalate to commercial leadership for approval.

Regards,
Priyom Das
Commercial Counsel, Redwood Inference
priyom_das@redwood.com
